reason: B's normalise_path pairs raw segments with segments of the decoded path, so an encoded %2F shifts the pairing and breaks R32/R33, while A splits on raw '/' only and decodes each segment separately.

Only A checks the whole item syntax (both endpoints and the step) before any numeric check and validates the base before the step; B checks the step first, C allows a step of width+1 in DayOfMonth/Month and checks step syntax after the base numbers, and D reports a bad right endpoint at the endpoint offset instead of the item start.

A accepts "-0" as an Integer, D returns Text("") instead of Null for a nullable empty Text cell, and B can panic on overflow for long decimals, while C has the correct grammar and uses checked arithmetic.

A computes the Escape offset with path.find(component), which finds the first '..' in the string rather than the one that escapes, while B tracks the real byte offset of each component, including after the tilde prefix.

A uses original offsets as cleaned indices in the CFWS boundary check and reports EmptyLabel before validating earlier labels, B reports TrailingLocal relative to the opening quote and puts the root-dot EmptyLabel at the wrong dot, and D returns an unmapped cleaned index for that EmptyLabel, while C maps runs and positions correctly.
B accepts tile value 1 because it is a power of two, though R5 requires 2..=2^31; A, C and D are otherwise equivalent and correct.

A does not count the first symbol after a wrap separator, so wrapped input with three or more rows fails, and it accepts a position-two '=' under Forbidden padding, while B's only gap is a whitespace byte directly after a separator.

D caps its integer square-root search near 2.83e9, so edge lengths over about 2.8e6 units are wrong, while A (like B and C) has exact half-up rounding, correct provenance, correct boundary ownership and correct Include/Exclude hulls.

A reports an empty interior component one byte early ("/a//b" gives 2, not 3) and C reports a trailing empty component at path.len() instead of the final slash, while B matches every R4 offset and the lookup error rules.
